Which European treaty first codified the principle of subsidiarity as both a broader political objective and a binding legal provision in Article 3b(2) ECT, serving as a barrier against misuse of Union competences?
questions.explanation: The Maastricht Treaty (1992) was the first EU treaty to formally enshrine subsidiarity in a dual form: as a general political goal and as a legally enforceable rule under Article 3b(2) of the EC Treaty. This provision was designed to prevent the Union from acting beyond its competences by requiring that action be taken at the EU level only where member states cannot sufficiently achieve the objectives themselves. Subsidiarity has since become a cornerstone principle of EU constitutional law.
